content:
Hi everyone! There have been a lot of discussions here about supporting different floating-point formats in Lean over the past couple of years, so I wanted to share FloatLib! Our original verified arithmetic in TorchLean focused on FP32. With FloatLib, we wanted to make that support much more general and reusable for applied mathematics (especially with all the PDE formalizations going on), numerical software and machine learning!

FloatLib supports arbitrary bit IEEE binary and decimal arithmetic, arbitrary-width posits, P3109, and low- precision formats including FP8, FP6, FP4, and block-scaled representations. You can also define your own formats and rounding rules, with different precisions for storage, multiplication, and accumulation. Each certified software backend carries a Lean proof that it returns the same result as its reference specification, including signed zeros and exceptional values. We also provides rounding, error-bound, and exactness theorems under their stated assumptions, including exact posit quire accumulation within capacity.

Speed was a design goal throughout. We use certified lookup tables for small formats, machine-word kernels, and limb algorithms for wider arithmetic. We’ve also compared numerical results and performance with established libraries including MPFR, Flocq, FLoPS, Berkeley SoftFloat/TestFloat, SoftPosit, and Universal.

It’s also great to see the logical models for Float32/64 introduced in Lean 4.33 and extended since then. Having these definitions available made it possible to connect numerical proofs to Lean’s native floating-point types. Both TorchLean and FloatLib are on 4.34 and TorchLean can now use any FP type from FloatLib!

Project details: https://leandojo.org/floatlib.html
More details here: X thread

Joint work with Will Adkisson and Anima Anandkumar. Thanks to the Lean, mathlib, and Flocq communities for the foundations we build on. Happy to answer any questions and suggestions/contributions welcome!
